rationale: This is an extremely small C++ program (49 lines, 5 functions, ~293 text bytes) whose logic is a recursive primes sieve with tiny class methods, so the priority is structural/control-flow diversity per byte rather than raw strength: SUB gets the highest emphasis on DiversityGain with minimal cost/risk weights because instruction substitution is nearly free and maximizes per-instruction entropy in already-tiny function bodies; SPLIT is boosted (DiversityGain 0.75, low costs) because splitting basic blocks enables and amplifies the effect of BCF/FLA on functions too small to obfuscate well otherwise; FLA and BCF carry solid SecurityGain weights but their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are kept moderate since flattening and bogus-branch inflation would dominate a 293-byte binary and the loop-heavy sieve/filter/counter methods are runtime-sensitive; ICALL is favored for DiversityGain (0.8, low size cost) because virtual/indirect call indirection on the sieve->filter->counter chain materially hides the dataflow graph at negligible size; IBR gets moderate weights as its indirect-jump overhead is acceptable only in main and the larger sieve::out, not the 10-byte counter::out; and IGV is kept in play at moderate weights since the sieve's state can be scattered, but is not emphasized given the program's minimal global-data footprint; CorrectnessRisk weights are uniformly low across the table because none of these passes threaten the simple, exception-free arithmetic at the core of this benchmark.
